text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called a "silent killer" because it typically causes no symptoms, and many people have it for years without knowing. You can learn more about general warning signs from the Mayo Clinic.
Symptoms of Dangerously High Blood Pressure
Symptoms generally only appear when blood pressure becomes severely elevated (a crisis or emergency, usually above 180/120 mmHg). At this stage, possible signs include:

list.snippet: Severe headaches or a feeling of a pounding in the head, neck, or ears
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Vision changes, such as blurred vision or eye pain
Nosebleeds or blood spots in the eyes
Swelling (edema) in the ankles, feet, or lower legs

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association, if your blood pressure reading is 180/120 mmHg or higher and you experience signs of organ damage—such as chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden back pain, numbness, weakness, or trouble speaking—call 911 immediately.
